About the Renderer

Technical details and architecture of the Vue 3 page renderer

intro.text:
What is the Vue 3 Page Renderer?

The Vue 3 Page Renderer is a modern replacement for the legacy Vue 2 renderer in Peregrine CMS. It provides the same core functionality—rendering JCR content as interactive Vue components—but built on Vue 3's improved architecture.

The renderer handles component registration, SPA navigation, edit mode detection, and seamless integration with Peregrine's admin console.

architecture.text:
Architecture

Core Components

  • peregrineApp.js — Main runtime handling app creation, navigation, and state management
  • PageModel.java — Sling Model for page-level properties and CSS/JS inheritance
  • Container.java — Sling Model for components with children
  • BaseComponentModel.java — Base Sling Model exporting text properties

Key Patterns

  • Composition API — Components use setup(), inject(), and computed()
  • Dependency Injection — Context provided via inject('peregrineApp')
  • Reactive State — Page state managed with Vue's reactive()

comparison.text:
Vue 2 vs Vue 3 Comparison

Key differences from the Vue 2 renderer:

  • API Style — Options API → Composition API
  • Reactivity — Object.defineProperty → Proxy-based
  • Context — this.$root → inject()
  • Module Format — Mixed IIFE → ES Modules
  • Build Tools — Rollup + Buble → Rollup + esbuild
